pairs.reason: Both are correct and well tested, and both handle float rounding and a clock that steps backwards. Implementation 2 is thread-safe and rejects an infinite refill rate, which matters for a shared client wrapper; Implementation 1 only documents that it is not thread-safe, and its typing is tidier.

Implementation 1 over-engineers the client with generic Protocol types, has no float tolerance, and moves its reference time back when the clock steps backwards, so that interval is credited again later. Implementation 2 handles those cases correctly but adds no tests at all, which makes it harder to merge and maintain.

Implementation 2 never checks that clock is callable and does not type-check tokens, so bad arguments raise TypeError instead of the required ValueError; it also has no float tolerance and re-credits time after the clock steps backwards. Implementation 1 handles all of these and its tests cover them.
